questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to take a good selfie
Whether phones will replace traditional cameras
The history of the very first phone with a digital camera
Why DSLR cameras are too expensive
questions.why: Neil asks whether cameras have been made obsolete by the smartphone.

questions.q: What happens when Neil tells Catherine to 'say cheese'?
options: He takes a nice photo of her
His phone camera doesn't work
He takes a selfie and she isn't in it
She refuses to be in the photo
questions.why: Catherine says 'You just took a selfie, I wasn't even in the picture.'

options: In her bag
At the studio
She doesn't have one
In a cupboard at home
questions.why: She says 'It's in a cupboard somewhere at home.'

questions.q: What is special about mirrorless cameras?
options: They are small but take the same lenses as DSLRs
They are the cheapest type of camera
They are only found on smartphones
They are fully automatic, with a fixed lens that can't be changed
questions.why: Neil says they're small like a compact but can use the same lenses as DSLRs.

questions.q: What does Phil Hall think about smartphones replacing cameras?
options: They already have
They will do so within a year
It won't happen completely any time soon
Only professional photographers will keep cameras
questions.why: He says he doesn't think the smartphone will take over the camera completely soon.

questions.q: Which cameras have seen the biggest fall in sales?
options: Cheap compact cameras
Mirrorless cameras
DSLRs
High-end premium cameras
questions.why: Phil Hall says compact camera sales have dropped off a cliff, especially cheap compacts.

questions.q: What are camera makers now focusing on?
options: Cameras for children
More expensive, high-end cameras
Making phones
Cheaper compact cameras for people on holiday
questions.why: Neil says camera makers are moving to the high-end market, DSLRs and mirrorless cameras.

questions.q: According to Phil Hall, why do some smartphone users buy a better camera?
options: Their phone is broken
Traditional cameras are now cheaper than most smartphones
Their friends tell them to
The quality frustrates them as their skills grow
questions.why: He says people get frustrated with the quality once they start pushing their creative skills.
